preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Alpine climate: -2°C to 26°C, cold winters. Smart casual, alpine gear for mountains.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: VIE (Vienna) primary hub. Austrian Airlines (flag carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: ÖBB (excellent).

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Austria-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Alpine continental. Vienna: -2°C (Jan) to 26°C (July). Salzburg: -4°C to 25°C. Alps: -10°C to 20°C. Winter skiing Dec-Mar. Pack layers, waterproof jacket, warm clothes for winter.

Apparel Sourcing: Smart casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Alpine/ski gear: Intersport, Hervis (local chains). Size system: European. Dirndl/Lederhosen for festivals (optional).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless widespread. CAT train to Vienna center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 98%, 5G extensive. ISPs: A1, Magenta Telekom, Drei. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: A1 (~€35/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous. Cash still used in small towns. No mobile money. Tipping: 5-10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Vienna VIE: CAT (City Airport Train) (€13, 16min) or S-Bahn S7 (€4.20, 25min). Official taxi: ~€50 to center. ÖBB trains to other cities.

mobility.simple: Vienna U-Bahn/S-Bahn/Bahn (extensive). No informal transit. Uber (limited, licensed taxis only). Citybike Wien. Excellent walkability, bike-friendly.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Vienna: U-Bahn (5 lines), S-Bahn, trams, buses. Integrated ticket (Wiener Linien). Salzburg: trolleybuses, buses. ÖBB trains between cities. Apps: WienMobil, Qando.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber restricted (licensed taxis only, no private cars). No Bolt. FreeNow taxi app. Bike-sharing: Citybike Wien (first hour free). E-scooters: Lime, Bird.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Dedicated bike lanes. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian priority at crossings. Very bike-friendly culture.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Mjam, Wolt, Lieferando. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Coffee house culture.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Mjam (Austrian), Wolt, Lieferando. Local: Frichti (meal kits). Grocery delivery: Billa, Spar. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, wine shops (Weinhandel). No state monopoly. Drinking age 16 for beer/wine, 18 for spirits. Wine culture (Grüner Veltliner). Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with red 'A'. Apotheken (pharmacies) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality (Alpine spring water). Zero-sugar options available. Local: Almdudler, Stroh. Coffee house culture (Viennese coffee). Schnitzel, strudel, Kaiserschmarrn.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Austrian breakfast buffets extensive. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), wine/chocolate OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants allowed). Punctuality, formal address, quiet demeanor.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Wine, chocolate, high-quality items appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants, cafes, public transport. Strict leash laws. Stray dogs rare.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, formality-focused. Formal address (Sie vs. Du). Punctuality essential (5-10 min early is on-time). Indirect communication. Tipping: 5-10% (round up). Personal space respected. Quiet in public. Coffee house culture central to social life. Hofbräu (court brewery) tradition.

preArrival.simple: Compare Paris and regional gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner; use AZair for low-cost European connections. Corsica needs a separate flight/ferry plan from mainland France.
preArrival.detailed:
National routing: Paris airports (CDG/ORY) and regional gateways serve different regions. Compare broad search with AZair for low-cost European legs, then verify train/airport transfer and baggage.

Corsica: Ajaccio (AJA), Bastia (BIA), Calvi (CLY), and Figari (FSC) serve different parts of the island. Compare seasonal flights with ferries from mainland ports; account for rental-car/coach access from arrival port.

Entry and climate: France is in Schengen; visa requirements depend on nationality and prior 90/180 days. Climate varies from Alpine to Mediterranean. Check regional weather and ferry/flight disruptions.

arrival24h.simple: France uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type E sockets. Corsica uses the same standard; check airport/ferry transfers for the specific island town.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type E sockets. Check grounded plug compatibility and device labels before use.

Connectivity and payments: Euro and contactless are common, but small venues may differ. Check roaming terms and rural/island coverage with your provider.

Airport transfer: Airport and station links vary by city. For Corsica, confirm ferry terminal/airport and local onward buses or car-rental availability before booking accommodation.

mobility.simple: SNCF connects mainland cities; Corsica has limited rail and seasonal buses. Check SNCF and Chemins de Fer de la Corse separately; car access is useful outside towns.
mobility.detailed:
Mainland: SNCF trains connect major cities; local transit is municipal. Check live timetables, reservation requirements, strikes, and station details before travel.

Corsica: Chemins de Fer de la Corse connects Ajaccio, Corte, and Bastia on a limited network. Bus frequency is lower outside peak season; check the current timetable and return service. A car may be useful for remote coves and villages.

Walking and driving: Historic centres may have restricted zones and cobbled streets. Corsican roads are winding; allow extra time and check seasonal ferry/road notices.

sources.topic: Chemins de Fer de la Corse

dailyLiving.simple: Deliveroo, Uber Eats, and grocery services cover many mainland cities; check exact address. Corsica has thinner, seasonal delivery coverage.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check Deliveroo/Uber Eats at your precise address; coverage falls in rural areas. In Corsica, plan groceries and pharmacy access before leaving larger towns.

Health and water: Follow municipal advisories and ask your accommodation about local supply/building notices. Pharmacies are marked pharmacie; check the duty-pharmacy listing and carry prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Try island specialties in Corsica and ask about ingredients/allergens. Euro is used. Service charges are shown on bills; additional tipping is discretionary.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting before requests; at religious sites, follow dress/photo rules. Corsica has distinct local traditions, so ask hosts rather than assuming Parisian customs.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings: A courteous bonjour/bonsoir before asking for help is a useful default. Use formal address in unfamiliar settings, then follow the other person's lead.

Home and religious visits: Ask about footwear and gifts. Follow posted rules at churches, museums, and memorials; ask permission before photographing people.

Corsica: Local language and community customs are distinct from mainland settings. Ask about preferences and respect private property, trails, and heritage sites.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Cool temperate climate: 0°C to 24°C. Casual dress, practical.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: FRA (Frankfurt), MUC (Munich), BER (Berlin) major hubs. Lufthansa (flag carrier), Eurowings. AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Germany-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Temperate continental. Berlin: 0°C (Jan) to 24°C (July). Munich: -2°C to 24°C. Hamburg: 1°C to 22°C. Rain year-round. Pack layers, waterproof jacket. Winter can be harsh in south (Alps).

Apparel Sourcing: Practical, casual style. Business casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Size system: European. Outdoor gear: Jack Wolfskin, Vaude (German brands).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless widespread. S-Bahn train FRA→city center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 150+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone, O2. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Telekom (~€40/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous (Girocard, credit cards). Cash still used in small towns (Germans prefer cash). No mobile money. PayPal common. Tipping: 5-10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Frankfurt FRA: S-Bahn S8/S9 (€4.65, 15min) or train (€9.75, 12min). Munich MUC: S-Bahn S1/S8 (€13.40, 45min). Berlin BER: Airport Express (€4.40, 30min) or regional train (€9.80, 20min).

mobility.simple: Extensive U-Bahn/S-Bahn networks. No informal transit. Uber (limited, licensed taxis only). Call a Bike, nextbike. Excellent walkability, bike-friendly.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Berlin: U-Bahn (9 lines), S-Bahn (15 lines), trams, buses. Munich: U-Bahn (8 lines), S-Bahn (8 lines). Integrated tickets (Deutschland-Ticket). Apps: DB Navigator, NVV, BVG.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber restricted (licensed taxis only, no private cars). No Bolt. FreeNow (MyTaxi) taxi app. Bike-sharing: Call a Bike (DB), nextbike, Lime. E-scooters: Tier, Lime, Voi.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Dedicated bike lanes (Fahrradwege) everywhere. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian priority at crossings. Very bike-friendly culture.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Lieferando, Wolt, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Pfand (deposit) on bottles.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Lieferando (Takeaway.com), Wolt, Uber Eats. Local: Frichti (meal kits). Grocery delivery: Rewe, Edeka. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, beverage shops (Getränkemarkt). No state monopoly. Drinking age 16 for beer/wine, 18 for spirits. Beer culture integral. Pfand (deposit) on bottles (€0.25).

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with red 'A'. Apotheken (pharmacies) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Club-Mate, Spezi. German bread culture. Bakeries ubiquitous.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. German breakfast buffets extensive. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), wine/chocolate OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants allowed). Punctuality, direct communication, recycling culture.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Wine, chocolate, high-quality items appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes (Hausschuhe) often provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants, cafes, public transport (muzzled in some cases). Strict leash laws. Stray dogs rare.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, punctuality-focused. Arrive on-time (5-10 min early is punctual). Direct communication valued. Formal vs. informal (Du/Sie) distinction. Tipping: 5-10% (round up). Personal space respected. Recycling mandatory (Pfand system). Quiet hours (Ruhezeit) 10pm-7am, Sundays.

preArrival.simple: Use AZair for low-cost European combinations and Google Flights/Skyscanner for broad coverage. Sardinia is a separate island-routing problem: compare Cagliari/Olbia/Alghero flights with ferries.
preArrival.detailed:
National routing: Rome (FCO), Milan (MXP/LIN), and other regional airports serve different itineraries. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with AZair and confirm baggage/airport with the operating airline.

Sardinia: Cagliari (CAG), Olbia (OLB), and Alghero (AHO) have different seasonal routes. Compare flights with ferries from mainland ports; use the island tourism/port operator timetable and include the port-to-lodging transfer.

Entry and climate: Italy is in Schengen; eligibility depends on nationality and prior 90/180 days. Weather varies from Alps to Mediterranean islands; check region-specific forecasts and pack layers.

arrival24h.simple: Italy uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type F and L sockets. Sardinia uses the same standard; compare airport/ferry transfer options and check local eSIM/roaming terms.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type F and L sockets. Check device compatibility and whether the accommodation offers grounded Type L outlets.

Connectivity and payments: Euro, cards, and contactless are common; keep cash for small merchants. Check roaming terms and rural coverage, especially in Sardinia's interior.

Arrival: Airport transport differs by city. In Sardinia, Cagliari, Olbia, and Alghero airports serve different areas; check current bus/car-rental/ferry connections with the airport/operator.

mobility.simple: Italy's rail system connects major cities; Sardinia relies more on regional ARST bus/rail and rental cars. Check Trenitalia/Italo and Sardinian operator schedules separately.
mobility.detailed:
Mainland: Trenitalia and Italo serve intercity routes; local transit is municipal. Verify station, train type, reservation, and ticket validation.

Sardinia: ARST runs regional buses and rail services; coverage/frequency is lower in inland areas. Check timetables and return services before day trips; a rental car may be necessary for remote beaches and villages.

Walking: Historic centers have cobbles and restricted-traffic zones (ZTL). Check signs and lodging access before driving; island terrain and summer heat affect walking.

dailyLiving.simple: Deliveroo, Glovo, and local grocery services cover many cities; check exact address. Sardinia island coverage varies by town and season.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Deliveroo and Glovo cover many urban areas; verify address and phone requirements. In Sardinia, service is concentrated in larger towns and may be seasonal.

Health and water: Tap-water guidance is municipal/building-specific; ask locally. Pharmacies are marked farmacia; check duty-pharmacy hours and bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Sardinia has distinct regional food traditions; ask about ingredients and allergens. Euro is used; service charges/coperto and tipping differ by venue, so read the bill.

socialCode.simple: At churches and archaeological sites, follow posted dress and photography rules. In Sardinia, ask about local customs and language preferences rather than assuming mainland norms.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small regional food gift is welcome. Household customs differ by family and region.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow signs on clothing, photography, and access. Ask before photographing people or private property.

Sardinia: Italian is widely used alongside Sardinian and other local varieties. Ask which language is preferred; respect community rules and protected sites.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Hot summers (35°C+), mild winters. Mediterranean dress, modest for churches.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: MAD (Madrid Barajas) and BCN (Barcelona El Prat) are primary hubs. AZair for European budget flights. Iberia, Vueling (IAG) major carriers. Ryanair and easyJet extensive European network.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Spain-Visa portal for eVisa applications.

Climate & Weather: Mediterranean continental. Madrid: 6°C (Jan) to 32°C (July). Barcelona: 9°C to 29°C. South (Seville): 11°C to 36°C (very hot summers). Pack for heat in summer, light layers.

Apparel Sourcing: Mediterranean casual style. Modest dress required for churches (shoulders/knees covered). Beachwear on beaches only. Summer: lightweight, breathable fabrics. Zara, Mango local brands.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless everywhere. Metro Express Line 8 MAD→center, express bus BCN.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets compatible. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 300+ Mbps download. 4G coverage 99%, 5G in major cities. ISPs: Movistar, Orange, Vodafone. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Movistar, Orange (~€30-40/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment nearly universal. Bizum (mobile money) popular for P2P transfers. Cash still used in small towns. Tipping: small amounts or round up.

Airport-to-City: Madrid: Metro Line 8 (€5, 15min to center) or Express Bus (€5, 40min). Barcelona: Aerobus (€5.90, 35min) or R2 train (€4.60, 25min). Official taxi: ~€30-35 to center.

mobility.simple: Madrid Metro (12 lines), Barcelona Metro (8 lines). Informal taxis. Uber/Cabify ride-hailing. Bicing bike share. Excellent walkability, hills in some cities.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Madrid Metro: 12 lines, 300+ stations, runs 6am-1:30am. Barcelona Metro: 8 lines, comprehensive network. Integrated transit cards: Metrobus (Madrid), T-Mobilitat (Barcelona). Apps: Citymapper, official transit apps.

Informal Transit: Limited formal alternatives. Some unofficial taxis, but regulated taxis dominate. No Matatus-style systems.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Cabify (Spanish), Uber (limited to major cities). Bike-sharing: Bicing (Barcelona), BiciMAD (Madrid). E-scooters: Lime, Bird, Yego.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Very walkable city centers. Pedestrian-only zones common. Hills in Barcelona (Catalan), Madrid relatively flat. Siesta affects midday activity (2-5pm).

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Glovo, Deliveroo, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Dining: late meals (9-11pm).
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Glovo (Spanish-founded), Deliveroo, Uber Eats. Local: Just Eat. Grocery delivery: Carrefour, Mercadona. Late-night delivery culture.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, bodegas, specialty shops. No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Wine and tapas culture central.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Strong prescription enforcement for antibiotics. Pharmacies marked with green cross. Some 24h pharmacies.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water safe and excellent. Zero-sugar options available. Local sodas: Kas, La Casera. Horchata in Valencia. Late meals: lunch 2-4pm, dinner 9-11pm.

Buffet Protocols: Mixed styles. Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional restaurants: one-plate with refills. Weight-based rare.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: flowers (odd numbers), wine/food. Shoes often removed in homes. Very dog-friendly. Personal space, physical touch in greetings, late schedules, meal times.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid yellow lilies (death). Wine or regional food (jamón, Manchego) excellent gifts. Host gifts expected for dinner invitations.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes, especially with hardwood floors. Follow host's lead.

Companion Pet Culture: Extremely dog-friendly. Dogs in restaurants, cafes, beaches (designated areas). Stray dogs rare in cities, more common in rural areas.

Behavioral Matrix: Warm, expressive culture. Personal space smaller than northern Europe. Physical greetings: two kisses (women-woman, women-man), handshake (men-men). Punctuality: 15-30 min grace socially. Late dining hours. Siesta still observed in smaller towns. Sunglasses outdoors only.

preArrival.simple: Direct booking on BA/easyJet. ETA required for most (free online). Maritime climate: 2°C to 22°C, rainy. Casual dress, pub culture.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: LHR (London Heathrow), LGW (Gatwick), MAN (Manchester) major hubs. British Airways (flag carrier), easyJet, Ryanair budget carriers. Direct booking typical. No regional consolidator standard.

Visa & Legal Compliance: ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) required for most visa-exempt nationalities (free online, 2 years). Visa required for others. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay. Not in Schengen.

Climate & Weather: Maritime. London: 2°C (Jan) to 22°C (July). Edinburgh: 1°C to 19°C. Rain year-round. Pack waterproof jacket, layers. Weather unpredictable (bring options).

Apparel Sourcing: Casual pub culture acceptable. Business attire in cities. Religious sites: modest dress. Size system: UK sizing (different from US/EU). Outdoor gear: Regatta, Berghaus (UK brands).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type G sockets (3 rectangular pins). 4G/5G excellent, eSIM available. NFC contactless ubiquitous. Heathrow Express/Elizabeth Line to London.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type G (British 3-pin) sockets with fuse. Unique to UK/Ireland/Malaysia/Singapore. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-g/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 80+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: EE, Vodafone, Three, O2. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: EE (~£30/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment universal (tap-to-pay, contactless cards limit £100). Apple Pay/Google Pay widely accepted. Cash declining but still used. No mobile money. Tipping: 10-15% for service.

Airport-to-City: London LHR: Heathrow Express (£25, 15min) or Elizabeth Line (£10.80, 45min). Gatwick: Gatwick Express (£19.80, 30min) or Southern train (£5.50, 45min). Black cabs (£60-80 to center).

mobility.simple: London Tube (11 lines), buses. No informal transit. Uber/Bolt ride-hailing. Santander Cycles. Excellent walkability, drive on left.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: London: Tube (11 lines), buses, DLR, Overground. Contactless payment (Oyster card or tap card). Manchester: Metrolink trams. Apps: TfL Go, Citymapper. **Drive on left**.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber, Bolt dominant. FreeNow (black cab app). Bike-sharing: Santander Cycles (London), Nextbike (other cities). E-scooters: Lime, Tier (trial zones only).

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability in cities. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian crossings: zebra crossings with Belisha beacons, cars must stop. Look right first when crossing (traffic from right).

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Deliveroo, Just Eat, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, pub hours 11am-11pm. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Pub culture.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Deliveroo, Just Eat, Uber Eats. Local: Frichti (London). Grocery delivery: Ocado, Tesco, Sainsbury's. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, off-licenses, pubs. No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Pub culture integral. Pubs close 11pm (some 1am). Service charge sometimes added.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies: Boots, Superdrug, Lloyds. Pharmacies in supermarkets (Tesco, Sainsbury's). 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: tea (with milk), beer (ale, stout), gin. Full English breakfast. Fish and chips.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Carvery buffets popular. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid white lilies (funerals), wine/chocolate OK. Shoes usually kept on. Dog-friendly (pubs allow). Queuing etiquette, politeness, understated humor.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: avoid white lilies (funerals). Odd numbers not significant. Wine, chocolate, high-quality items appropriate. Host gifts appreciated. Presentation modest.

Household Norms: Shoes usually kept on, unless muddy. Follow host's lead.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in pubs (patios, some indoors). Service dogs allowed everywhere. Stray dogs rare. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, politeness-focused. Queuing culture (queue jumping taboo). 'Please', 'thank you', 'sorry' used frequently. Indirect communication (understated). Punctuality: 5-10 min grace socially. Tipping: 10-15% for service (optional if service charge added). Personal space respected. Pub culture central to social life. Humor: dry, self-deprecating.
